title: Pagerless Escalation and Shadow Ops Handbook
author: Maya Patel
body:
Overview

This handbook documents the Pagerless Escalation pattern and the Shadow Ops role used for low- and medium-severity degradations where immediate interrupting pages are unnecessary or counterproductive. It defines the decision criteria, communication templates, role responsibilities, automated signals, and game-day exercises to validate the pattern.

Why we use pagerless escalation
- Reduce alert fatigue for noisy, transient signals (e.g., short-lived 5xx bursts, KV cache warm-up spikes).
- Reserve pagers for incidents requiring synchronous coordination (high-severity/Customer-impacting).
- Improve signal triage fidelity by enriching alerts with context before human interrupt.

Scope
- Applies to Redwood-hosted runtime and Dedicated control-plane alerts categorized as Severity 3 and Severity 4 in our incident taxonomy.
- Does NOT apply to: security breaches, data-loss events, full-region outages, or SLA-violating incidents (Severity 1 or 2).

Key concepts and definitions
- Pagerless Alert: An automated alert that posts to #ops-notifications with a synthesized summary, suggested runbook link, and a list of likely remediation steps. No pager is fired automatically.
- Shadow Ops: A rotating, lightweight operative (not full responder) who monitors pagerless alerts, performs preliminary analysis, and escalates when human coordination is required.
- Mobilization Bridge: A temporary collaboration channel (Slack huddle + Zoom bridge) opened when escalation criteria are met.

Roles and responsibilities
| Role | Primary responsibilities | Escalation contact |
| Shadow Ops | Monitor pagerless alerts, confirm signal validity, attempt quick mitigations, update status doc | Primary oncall (if escalated) |
| Shadow Lead (senior) | Final decision to escalate to bridge, coordinate customer comms if needed | SRE oncall, Incident Commander |
| Primary Oncall | Runs bridge, coordinates engineers, executes major mitigations | Engineering oncall roster |
| Customer Success | Prepare customer-facing notices if bridge opens | Customer Success Manager |

Decision criteria: when to remain pagerless vs escalate
1. Stay pagerless when all of the following are true:
   - Incident classified Severity 3 or 4.
   - Signal includes a clear, single-service scope (not cross-region).
   - Estimated customer impact < 5% of active requests or limited to internal telemetry.
   - Automated mitigations or cache warming can be attempted without cross-team coordination.
2. Escalate to a Mobilization Bridge when any of the following occur:
   - Error rate sustains > 10% for 5 minutes after automated throttles/buffering.
   - SLO for critical path (p99 latency or availability) is projected to be breached within 15 minutes.
   - Multiple services begin failing concurrently or multiple customers report matching errors.

Pagerless flow (step-by-step)
1. Detection: Alerting platform (Prometheus/Alertmanager) fires a pagerless alert into #ops-notifications and creates an incident stub in the incident tracker (Jira/IR-XXXX). Alert contains: concise summary, core metrics (30s/5m/1h), top 3 correlated traces, proposed runbook link.
2. Auto-enrichment: Alert processor attaches recent traces, mapping to model-serving shard, last deploy, and recent kernel/quantization changes.
3. Shadow Ops pickup (within 3 minutes): Rotating Shadow Ops acknowledges the alert in Slack and updates the incident stub with initial triage notes.
4. Quick mitigations (if applicable, within 10 minutes): Restart worker pool on affected shard, enable fallback model variant, purge stale cache prefix. Shadow Ops documents commands used.
5. Observe (10–30 minutes): If metrics recover to < threshold for 15 minutes, mark incident as "resolved without pager" and close stub after a 1-hour observation window.
6. Escalate: If criteria in "Decision criteria" are met, Shadow Ops notifies Shadow Lead and requests bridge. The Shadow Lead confirms and triggers pager and bridge.

Templates and automation
- Slack message template (pagerless alert to #ops-notifications):
  > [pagerless] IR-XXXX | service: runtime-ingest | 5xx rate 7.2% (5m) | affected region: us-west-2 | suggested mitigations: restart-pool, enable-fallback-model | link: <incident-stub-link>

- Incident stub fields (minimum):
  - title (string)
  - severity (S1..S4)
  - observed_at (ISO timestamp)
  - affected_services (CSV)
  - initial_metric_snapshot (30s/5m/1h)
  - enrichment_links (traces, logs, recent-deploys)
  - actions_taken (chronological bullet list)

Runbook excerpt: common quick mitigations
1. Restart worker pool (stateless replicas):
   - CLI: rdxctl cluster restart --service runtime-ingest --shard X
   - Expected result: drop in 5xx within 60–120s as unhealthy nodes recycle
2. Enable fallback model variant:
   - Console: model -> runtime-ingest -> Switch to variant fallback-v1
   - Note: fallback reduces quality but often restores availability quickly
3. KV cache purge for prefix storm:
   - CLI: rdx-cachectl purge --prefix project123:prompt_cache --region us-west-2
   - Caution: large purges may cause CPU spikes; stagger if > 10M keys

Customer communication guidance (pagerless incidents)
- If resolved without pager: No external communication required. Document internally and include a one-paragraph summary in the weekly operations digest.
- If bridge opens or incident affects > 5% of customers: Customer Success drafts an outbound notice using the template below and coordinates approval with Shadow Lead.

Customer notice template (short outage)
Subject: Redwood Inference brief impact to request processing in us-west-2
Body: We observed elevated error rates for request processing in us-west-2 between 2026-11-15 03:12 UTC and 2026-11-15 03:32 UTC. Our automated mitigations (pool restart and fallback model enable) restored service. We do not expect data loss. If you saw degraded responses, please contact your CSM.

Status page messaging (when bridge opens)
- Status title: Elevated error rates in us-west-2 (Runtime Ingest)
- Impact: Some customers may experience increased errors and latency.
- Current status: Investigating (Engineering mobilized)
- Next update cadence: Every 20 minutes until mitigation confirmed

Game day exercises (to validate the pattern)
1. Objective: Validate that Shadow Ops can detect, mitigate, and decide not to escalate for a synthetic Severity 3 event.
2. Injected signal: Simulate a 5xx spike on a single shard for 12 minutes.
3. Success criteria:
   - Shadow Ops acknowledges within 3 minutes
   - Quick mitigations executed within 8 minutes and documented
   - No bridge opened and incident closed after 1-hour observation window
4. Post-exercise deliverable: 1-page summary, runbook adjustments, and lessons learned logged to the incident learning catalog.

Rotation and coverage guidance
- Shadow Ops is a 1-week rotating role drawn from oncall teams. Typical rotation: Mon 00:00 UTC to Mon 00:00 UTC.
- Shift responsibilities: 30-minute response SLA to acknowledge; 10-minute SLA to attempt allowed quick mitigations.
- Training: New Shadows complete an onboarding lab focused on common mitigation commands and the alert enrichment UI.

Metrics and reporting
- Tracked KPIs (weekly):
  - Pagerless incident count
  - Pagerless escalation rate (percentage that required bridge)
  - Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for pagerless alerts
  - % of pagerless incidents that later become S1/S2 (should be < 1%)

Postmortem and learning cadence
- Any pagerless incident that escalates to bridge must follow the standard postmortem template (timeline, detection path, root cause, action items).
- Quarterly synthesis: Operations synthesizes recurring pagerless themes and recommends runbook/alert tuning.

Runbook governance and review
- Owners must review Shadow Ops runbooks annually or after any escalated incident.
- Shadow Lead runs monthly quick-practice drills and reports drift or stale commands to the runbook owner.

Appendix A — Quick checklist for Shadow Ops (printable)
1. Read alert summary and incident stub.
2. Confirm recent deploys and top correlated traces.
3. Attempt quick mitigation (choose 1): restart-pool, enable-fallback, purge-prefix.
4. Update incident stub with time-stamped actions.
5. Observe for 10–30 minutes. If recovery, mark resolved-without-pager and close after observation window.
6. If criteria met, notify Shadow Lead and request bridge.

Appendix B — Runbook links and automation endpoints
- Incident tracker template: https://jira.internal/redwood/IR-XXXX
- Alert enrichment UI: https://opsui.internal.redwood/alerts/enriched
- Pagerless automation config (example):
  {
    "alert_type": "pagerless",
    "escalate_thresholds": {"error_rate_pct": 10, "slo_projection_minutes": 15},
    "shadow_ack_timeout_s": 180
  }
